hook_text: Johannesburg to Durban: ten centimetres on the map. How many kilometres is that?
clip_script: Johannesburg, planning a holiday on the map. Method one: a ruler. Johannesburg to Durban measures ten centimetres. The word scale says one centimetre represents fifty kilometres. Ten times fifty: about five hundred kilometres. Method two: a paper strip. Mark both cities on the edge, lay it on the line scale from zero, and read the distance. That is the straight-line distance, as the crow flies. By road, it is longer: about five hundred and seventy kilometres.
visual_style: Whiteboard map of South Africa with a ruler between Johannesburg and Durban, then a paper strip sliding onto a line scale.
mood: Practical and confident, like a navigator planning a trip.
pacing: Clear step-by-step measuring, a quick calculation, then the road-distance twist.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and measure the straight-line distance from your town to the nearest big city.
